strategies.name: Baseline Unrolled All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Direct translation of the seed code: 8 all-reduce dispatches, each preceded by a forward bidiagonal coupling pass and followed by a backward decoupling pass. Total 8 all-reduce dispatches on full (W*S) tensors. Represents the simplest correct approach with maximum dispatch overhead but minimal algorithmic complexity.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with reduce-scatter (producing local shard) followed by all-gather. This enables applying the bidiagonal coupling/decoupling only to local shards between stages, reducing local compute from O(W*S) to O(S) per stage. Total 16 dispatches (8 reduce-scatter + 8 all-gather) but ~W times less local computation per iteration.

strategies.name: Fused Bidiagonal Transform All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Merge the forward coupling and division into a single pre-processing step, then single all-reduce, then backward decoupling as post-processing. Repeat 8 times but with tighter fusion boundaries to enable compiler optimization of the compute kernels between collectives. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but improved arithmetic intensity and potential XLA fusion.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction
strategies.desc: Exploit multi-node topology by performing intra-node all-reduce (28 ranks/node × 8 nodes) followed by inter-node reduction and broadcast. Apply bidiagonal transforms at node granularity to reduce cross-node traffic. Approximately 8×(1 intra-node AR + 1 inter-node reduce + 1 inter-node broadcast) = 24 dispatches but with smaller inter-node payloads.

strategies.name: Pipelined Overlapped Chunked Execution
strategies.desc:
Partition the W*S vector into K chunks and pipeline the 8-stage loop: while stage i processes chunk j, stage i+1 processes chunk j-1. Use non-blocking collectives (if available) or manual chunking to overlap communication and local bidiagonal arithmetic. Same 8 all-reduce count asymptotically but enables latency hiding through spatial chunking and temporal pipelining.
